headline: OLED iPad mini 8 debuting this week, marking its first overhaul since 2021
summary: Apple's compact tablet is set for a significant update, reportedly featuring a new OLED display and expected price details to be revealed alongside its debut.
details: Apple is reportedly preparing to launch the iPad mini 8 this week, marking the first major overhaul for the compact tablet since 2021. The most significant upgrade is expected to be a new OLED display, enhancing visual quality and power efficiency.

While specific details on pricing and full specifications are yet to be officially confirmed, the report from 9to5Mac suggests these will be revealed shortly. This update aims to refresh the iPad mini's appeal in the competitive tablet market.

headline_marked: [[UC Berkeley math professor]] stops grading homework due to AI use
headline: UC Berkeley math professor stops grading homework due to AI use
summary: A Fields medalist professor has abandoned traditional homework grading, citing widespread AI use among students and questioning the future of mathematics.
details: Richard Borcherds, a distinguished UC Berkeley mathematics professor and Fields medalist, has stopped grading his students' homework for correctness. He cited the widespread and consistent use of AI tools by students to achieve top scores as the reason, stating there was "no point" in continuing the practice.

This decision comes in the wake of significant advancements in AI, including OpenAI's AI agents reportedly solving a major unsolved problem in mathematics. Borcherds expressed concern that if AI continues its current rate of improvement, human mathematicians may soon be unable to perform tasks that AI cannot do better.

Currently, Borcherds grades homework based solely on completion, admitting it's "not a very good system" but lacking a viable alternative. He is unsure how to advise students on pursuing mathematics as a career, a field once considered safe from the AI revolution.

Even ChatGPT, when asked for advice on career paths in mathematics amidst AI advancements, reportedly stated it had no clear answers. Borcherds noted the academic system's inertia, comparing the situation to the slow adoption of digital publishing over physical journals.

While UC Berkeley encourages faculty to include AI use policies in syllabi, the specifics vary by course. The campus has found AI detection tools inadequate for standardization, leaving AI policy largely to individual faculty discretion.
